# Runtime and memory

Edva lowers to LLVM IR and uses an arena-managed runtime for dynamic values.
Types are checked statically and erased at runtime. A function value is exactly
`{ fn_ptr, env_ptr }`; it has no type tag or runtime signature information.

## Strings and Builders

`String` is immutable. `?string` returns its byte length and `&string` its
data address (RawPtr). Strings have no `.len` or `.data` members. `Builder` is the
mutable buffer type: `{capacity}` creates one, `builder += value` appends, and
`+builder` freezes it into an immutable String in place. `?builder = n` sets its
recorded length, which is useful after an FFI read into `&builder`.

## Errors and fallible operations

`Error` is a core record used as the negative payload of fallible operations.
It is poisonous: constructing it is inert only in an error slot; unwrapping an
Error aborts and prints diagnostic information. Array indexing and map lookup
return a ram; use `result!!` when abort-on-error is intended, or route the
ram through a choice when its alternatives require different work.

## Foreign boundaries and lifetimes

`Addr` is the raw address type for FFI. Pass a String or Builder buffer with
the adjacent unary `&` form, such as `&buffer`. Arena-backed addresses and views
have bounded lifetimes—do not retain them across an arena restore or store a
non-escaping address in a longer-lived value. Consult the
[FFI and targets guide](../../guide/ffi-and-targets.qmd) and the relevant
standard-library bindings as the detailed reference.
